title: ACL reconstruction
what: Through small cuts, the surgeon replaces the torn knee ligament with a new one. It is made from one of your own tendons.
why: For a torn ligament when the knee is unstable and gives way, and you want to return to sports and activity.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours, with 1 to 3 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
Past blood clots in the veins
What sport you play and what you expect from surgery

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Knee
prepare.text: Before surgery, you are often advised to get the knee moving and the swelling down. Do the exercises your doctor gave you.

prepare.title: Crutches
prepare.text: Ask in advance if you need crutches and a brace. Best to learn to use them before surgery.

bring: Your referral, MRI scans, and test results
Crutches and a brace, if you were told to buy them
steps: On the day, you change, and an IV line is placed
The anesthetist gives general or spinal anesthesia
The surgeon takes a tendon for the new ligament through a small cut
A camera and instruments go in through small openings
The new ligament is passed through the bone and fixed in place
The openings are stitched, and a bandage and brace go on the leg
feel: The knee hurts and swells. You will get painkillers and cold packs
The spot where the tendon was taken may also ache
after: Rehab starts almost right away. It is the main part of treatment
You usually walk on crutches for a few weeks
Cold and a raised leg reduce swelling
Running usually comes back after a few months, sports later, as your doctor decides
red_flags: Pain and swelling in the calf, or the leg feels hot
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus from the wounds
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: When can I go back to sports?
faq.a: Usually not before 6 to 9 months. Your doctor and physical therapist decide based on tests.
Sometimes, if your activity level is low. You decide together with your surgeon.

reminders.text: Knee surgery tomorrow. Bring your scans, documents, crutches, and brace. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
